name: Legacy ASL fingerspelling prototype
description: Hand-tuned rules for American Sign Language (ASL) letters A-Z, ported from the original single-page prototype. It is not Indian Sign Language.
limitations: ASL, not ISL: it does not recognise Indian Sign Language.
Hand-tuned geometric rules, not a trained model; no documented evaluation exists.
Scores are rule scores, not probabilities or accuracy.
One hand, static handshapes only; letters that need movement are not handled as movement.
Not suitable for medical, legal, emergency or other high-stakes communication.

name: Experimental ISL (trained by you in this browser)
description: Nearest-neighbour matching over samples that a user records in their own browser. It has no built-in classes: it only knows the signs that user recorded, and the samples never leave the device.
limitations: Not a validated ISL model: no trained weights ship and no evaluation exists.
Recognises only the signs the current user recorded, as that user performed them.
The class count is 0 on the server because classes exist only in the browser of the person who recorded them.
Scores are similarity scores, not probabilities or accuracy.
Static signs only; signs that depend on movement are out of scope.
Not suitable for medical, legal, emergency or other high-stakes communication.

name: Simulator (synthetic landmarks)
description: Feeds synthetic hand landmarks through the interface so it can be tried without a camera. It is a demonstration of the interface, not recognition.
limitations: Output is generated, not recognised from a person signing.
Says nothing about recognition quality for any sign language.
The class count is recorded as 0 because the simulator has no trained classes.
